claim: Before applying a Catmull-Clark Subdivision Surface modifier, select the edges that should stay sharp or flat and use Shift+E (Edge Crease) to drag a partial or full crease into them -- this preserves hard/flat regions without needing separate bevel geometry, and can be tuned continuously rather than being all-or-nothing.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (4:17-4:51): "before we actually apply the subdivision surface what we're going to do and this is the part that i didn't know for the longest time... we're going to select the edges that we want to keep sharp um and then i'm going to hit shift e and we can drag and sharpen these edges and they don't even need to be all the way sharp or we can make them totally flat"

claim: For a 3D-print target, chose Subdivision Surface viewport/render level 4 over level 5 -- level 5 looked marginally smoother but produced an unnecessarily large vertex count, while level 4 was judged 'still super smooth' and a more realistic vertex count for slicing/printing.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (5:26-6:16): "i'm going to crank this up let's do five let's do five ooh that is smooth... yeah that still might be a lot of vertices all right all right all right all right lesson learn lesson learn let's go back to four still super smooth... now we're at a realistic number of vertices for 3d printing"
reason: Level 5 added vertex count with no meaningful visible smoothness gain over level 4 for a physical print, and higher vertex counts risk slicer/printer problems.

claim: The 'On Cage' display option in Edit Mode snaps the visible edit-mode wireframe onto the modifier's predicted subdivided surface instead of showing the pre-subdivision control cage -- toggling it is a quick way to check where edits will actually land on the smoothed result before applying the modifier.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (3:23-3:39): "if you go into tab into edit mode uh you can click this on cage this is going to snap your current faces onto the predicted subdivided face". Visually confirmed (2026-08-14) via Gemini video understanding on the actual video at this timestamp: before toggling, the edit-mode wireframe shows as a separate low-poly cage surrounding the smoothed surface; after toggling On Cage, the wireframe/vertices visibly snap directly onto the contoured subdivided surface; toggling off reverts to the separate outer cage -- matches the claim precisely, upgraded from the earlier caveat about imprecise narration.
